kiln_p16_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_001.text: The ash yard had been swept before the hearing, but a gray edge remained where rain had carried the fine dust beneath the wall. Chairs stood on boards so that nobody would sit with their feet in mud. The reviewer wanted a place close enough to the workshop for the practical records and separate from the active kiln. Yue arrived with her account and found Jian beside his mother, not behind the machinery where he usually looked confident. Han sat near the exit with room for his injured arm. An ordinary arrangement of chairs had made every consequence visible.

kiln_p16_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_002.text: The chair explained the hearing's scope before taking accounts. The immediate safety finding, employment limits and apprenticeship remedy would be decided from the evidence and current workshop rules. Compensation questions beyond the owner's existing care and customer arrangements would use the appropriate civil process. Nobody would have a disputed family obligation invented in this yard. Public apprenticeship questions would receive their own response even if the boy's act was established. Yue watched several people straighten at that last sentence. They had feared either that sympathy would erase the vent alteration or that blame would erase everything which preceded it.

kiln_p16_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_003.text: Peng presented the physical sequence first. The authorised pre-firing check showed the pin seated and the shutter within its rated travel. Later evidence showed removal with gripping-tool marks, a wedge in the frame and movement beyond the stop. Interrupted process readings, ware positions and operator accounts described the resulting condition. She identified which observations were direct and which conclusions depended on comparison. The wedge was displayed cold behind a simple boundary. It looked too small to bear the weight the room gave it. Yue remembered the boy making ordinary movements with ordinary hands and felt her throat tighten.

kiln_p16_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_004.text: Jian's corrected account followed without a theatrical demand to stand above everyone. He described taking the tool, removing the pin, placing the wedge, seeing the larger movement and leaving instead of restoring it. The chair asked whether he had heard the danger and scope lesson beforehand. He answered yes. He had believed the warnings would limit any unexpected change. The chair asked whether the crew had agreed to take that risk. He answered no. His mother looked at the floor while he said it. Yue kept her eyes on the record, where the words would remain after his voice stopped.

kiln_p16_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_005.text: The outside runner clarified the figure she had seen near the passage. She could identify a younger worker's clothing, not his face with certainty. The hearing did not transform her partial observation into a perfect identification because a confession now existed. Her account remained useful for the timing it actually supported. Tan's receiving runner likewise confirmed the door transaction and approximate interval without pretending to have watched the vent continuously. Yue found these modest limits reassuring. A finding supported by several bounded accounts could be stronger than a polished story in which every witness suddenly saw everything.

kiln_p16_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_006.text: Luo showed the cold model used in the earlier lesson. He explained how excess draft could increase combustion in one region while chilling another, carry hot grit and defeat the comparison assumptions. The learner had not been taught a safe live fault-making method. No such permission existed. He described the rated stops and response delay, then named the warning obstruction and credit confusion the hall had already corrected. His own history entered the record alongside Jian's agency. The foreman sounded older than he had beside the flames, perhaps because here the danger was a sentence he could not simply close.

kiln_p16_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_007.text: The apprenticeship representative asked whether the boy's cold knowledge had ever been checked rather than merely spoken at him. Peng produced his accurate cold explanation and supervised exercises. They did not qualify him to alter a live vent; they showed that the relevant boundary had been understood. The representative then asked about his general inspection request. Its submission, acknowledgment and interim answer predated the fire. The visiting review was still scheduled later because of staffing and circuit duties. Those limitations were genuine and could be questioned. They were not evidence that the ordinary path had been wholly closed.

kiln_p16_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_008.text: Yue gave her witnessed account of the inspection conversation and her explicit refusal to support an invented hazard. She did not include a clever argument she wished she had made afterward. The chair asked what Jian had said about fire. She supplied the words and uncertainty from her same-day note. She could testify to the question, not to every private intention forming behind it. Jian listened with his hands open on his knees. Afterward he asked permission to confirm that she had not encouraged him. His statement was recorded without turning her into the person responsible for stopping future choices.

kiln_p16_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_009.text: Han spoke after a short rest. He described the hot grit at his sleeve edge, the warning he followed and the ordinary care since. The burn was small in area and real in pain, restricted work and interrupted sleep. He refused both an exaggerated claim of permanent ruin and a dismissive account of a trivial mark. He did not know whether there would be any lasting change; the clinician would assess that as recovery progressed. Jian stared at him throughout. Yue saw how difficult it was to hear harm measured accurately when guilt wanted either catastrophe or easy reassurance.

kiln_p16_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_010.text: The care worker provided the current restrictions with Han's permission. Dressing changes, review appointments and temporary exclusion from the hot post were needed. Modified cold work was possible within the care limits. The owner had funded treatment and preserved contracted wages rather than charge recovery to the worker. The worker's future clearance would depend on healing, not the hearing's desire for an ending. Han asked that this line stay in the public decision. He did not want a notice saying the matter was settled while his arm still needed care. The chair agreed, and the clerk added the condition.

kiln_p16_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_011.text: The cooperative customer described the accepted jars, the shortage and the amended transport arrangement. Her extra cart trip was documented rather than guessed. She appreciated the temporary approved containers and still wanted the remaining jars on the new schedule. The clinic representative gave a similarly practical account of the pots. Neither had purchased an apprenticeship debate. The owner accepted the material and delivery duties already agreed. Yue had expected customers to arrive angry in the same way. Their concerns differed: dry seed, reliable clinic stock, missed travel time. The incident had entered several lives through different ordinary doors.

kiln_p16_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_012.text: Zhu presented the ware inspection. The preexisting rejected jar remained excluded from the loss. Fresh thermal cracks, roughened hot-zone surfaces and unaffected pieces were listed separately. The qualified body had not become inherently unsuitable because the live process changed. The repaired retainer had passed current cold and guarded checks, permitting a defined ordinary schedule rather than universal immunity. Zhu spoke with the calm she used when measuring a rim, then lost that calm when someone called the remaining pieces lucky. Their survival had positions and conditions, she said. Luck was a poor label for information workers still needed.

kiln_p16_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_013.text: The owner explained the incident account without hiding the numbers beneath a promise. Care, remakes and transport had assigned workshop funding. Contracted wages remained due. Any discretionary bonus depended on the published profit rule, with the actual expense disclosed. She accepted that earlier informal credit arrangements had contributed to learners' mistrust, and described the remedies already underway. She did not claim that these errors caused the boy's deliberate alteration. Responsibility could be divided according to actual acts without becoming a contest over who must carry the entire winter. Yue watched Jian's mother listen to every ordinary amount.

kiln_p16_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_014.text: Jian was invited to explain his motive after the operational accounts. He wanted an outside team to inspect now and believed a visible fault would compel it. He had expected spoiled ware and a stopped firing, not injury. He understood now that he had relied on other people responding to a risk they never agreed to take. The chair asked why he had not waited for the desk answer. He said waiting felt like becoming the kind of learner whose letters stayed unanswered forever. His promised qualification date made waiting unbearable. The live vent still belonged to the crew.

kiln_p16_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_015.text: His mother described the relevant permitted household letters. She had repeated his hopeful date to relatives; she had not told him to make the workshop fail. She wanted a safe path for him to earn wages and continue learning, but would not call the act an accident. Her voice cracked at that word. Yue saw Jian move as if to comfort her and stop because the room was still taking evidence. The mother's account did not solve the punishment question. It prevented a convenient story in which family poverty had issued an invisible order.

kiln_p16_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_016.text: The chair asked about alternative actions available at the time. The request, alternate contact and review date were real, though imperfect. Paid supported submissions were now clearer; the earlier allowance had been less explicit. Jian could have sought help from the representative, corrected the overstated qualification letter or refused an unsafe assignment had one been given. He had not been assigned this alteration. The distinction hurt because the alternatives required patience and embarrassment rather than dramatic leverage. Yue understood why they had felt weaker to him. He stared at the retained answer while the clerk read the alternatives again.

kiln_p16_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_017.text: At midday the hearing paused. Han went to rest, customers returned to their work and the clerk checked the accounts against the retained packet. Nobody could tell Yue the decision. She carried a simple lunch to Jian and his mother, leaving it on the bench without demanding conversation. He asked whether he had spoken too much about the letters. She said the chair would weigh the relevant facts; a motive did not become better through repetition. He ate slowly. Beyond the wall an ordinary firing continued under the revised checks. The sound of work felt almost cruel in its steadiness.

kiln_p16_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_018.text: Zhu joined Yue near the drying racks. She said she wanted the boy kept far from the live vent and also wanted the apprenticeship claim answered. She was tired of being asked which wish mattered more. Yue agreed. The two issues shared a history but required different work. 'Will your fourth pair solve that?' Zhu asked. Yue laughed too sharply, then apologized. Her current new task could move a quarter useful unit under supervision. It could not move other people's obligations into a single comfortable place, no matter how many routes she eventually earned.

kiln_p16_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_019.text: The reviewer returned with a preliminary finding and allowed specific factual corrections before the decision. Jian's deliberate unauthorised alteration was supported by the physical evidence and his corroborated account. The act created an uncontrolled condition outside the rated process, causing the recorded injury, material damage and delay. His intended scale and inspection motive were recognized without making the risk consensual. Earlier institutional weaknesses and subsequent corrections would remain in the separate general review. Peng checked one delivery date and corrected it. The chair welcomed the correction. Accuracy remained possible even when most of the finding was painful.

kiln_p16_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_020.text: The workshop consequence barred Jian from live operation and unsupervised access to the hot control passage during a defined review period. His paid cold role would have named tasks, supervision and a check after eight weeks. Reinstatement was not automatic at that date. It required demonstrated safe practice, truthful reporting and an independent recommendation, with the affected worker's safety concerns heard. His old completed cold exercises remained valid within their original scope. Final apprenticeship qualification was deferred until the required supervised course and assessment could be completed. The boy listened as time became something more specific than an endless disgrace.

kiln_p16_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_021.text: The owner would not impose hidden wage deductions for the loss. Any personal compensation finding required the proper process and actual means, not an invented hereditary debt. He could offer voluntary useful remedy within paid safe work, but it would not purchase forgiveness or live access. The owner had duties to injured workers and customers regardless of whether recovery from the boy was later ordered. Yue watched his mother breathe for the first time since the consequence began. The practical boundary did not lessen the seriousness of the act; it kept seriousness from becoming limitless power over a household.

kiln_p16_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_022.text: The remedy required more than repeating warnings. Jian would study incident sequences, explain control boundaries in new examples and complete observed cold tasks where a changed condition demanded a stop rather than a clever improvisation. A qualified teacher would assess those tasks, and an independent reviewer would consider later access. The boy could challenge ferrors through the stated route. The plan had actual funded hours and an employer willing to provide safe work during the period. It was demanding without pretending that suffering itself taught the missing lesson. Jian asked for the teacher hours in writing and read them twice.

kiln_p16_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_023.text: Han asked about declining a shared hot shift if Jian eventually regained clearance. The owner said his concern would be considered in the roster and safety review, without promising that every preference could rule the entire shop forever. Current care restrictions already excluded the hot post. The chair added that no reconciliation meeting was required to finish the hearing. An offered apology remained an offer. Jian looked at Han and said he understood. Yue hoped the understanding would survive the slow weeks when the sentence no longer felt new and the unanswered friendship hurt more sharply.

kiln_p16_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_024.text: The general apprenticeship review received its own actions: a public cold sample visit, interviews with current and former learners, independent credit checks and a summer practical observation. The visiting team's time would not be expanded by pretending the urgent hazard reviewer had unlimited duties. Interim questions with adequate documents would receive dated desk responses. The owner assigned paid preparation hours and preserved access to corrected records. Zhu asked that unfinished claims be listed rather than called resolved by the new forms. The chair agreed. The public concern Jian had distorted could still be addressed without danger.

kiln_p16_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_025.text: The revised fixture and warning controls remained under their separate technical schedule. The hall would retain the old fitting, dated drawings, checks and damaged sample map. Future alteration required an approved design and guarded qualification; an apprentice's persuasive explanation would not suffice. Luo asked the clerk to record that this rule applied to senior workers too. Tan glanced at his own contract folder and nodded. Yue appreciated the foreman's insistence. A boundary aimed only at the youngest worker would teach obedience to status rather than the relation between a changed mechanism and the actual people exposed to its failure.

kiln_p16_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_026.text: The final decision was read aloud with the correction and appeal route. Jian could ask for factual review within the stated period, and new evidence could be submitted without secretly changing the retained account. He signed that he had received the decision, not that signing erased his right to question an error. His mother received the employment and care boundaries in a separate plain summary. Yue received only the parts relevant to her witnessed account and support role. The room emptied unevenly. Some people wanted to talk, some wanted a cart home, and Han wanted another ordinary afternoon of rest.

kiln_p16_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_027.text: Jian stood beside the empty chair after his mother left. He said eight weeks sounded both too long and not enough. Yue answered that the review date measured the next check, not the whole value of his life. He asked whether she thought he could learn the required restraint. She said he had already learned mechanisms and records; choosing limits under pressure would need practice too. She would not promise the result. He nodded, less frightened by the uncertainty than he had been by her earlier anger. A future without a guarantee had become more believable.

kiln_p16_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_028.text: Han stopped at the yard boundary and asked Jian to keep the exact account when people tried to improve it. The boy agreed. Han did not touch his shoulder or offer a joke. Yue watched the ordinary distance between them and resisted closing it with words. The hearing could not order their friendship to heal as quickly as skin. When Han left, Jian remained facing the gate until his mother called him. The absence of a warm scene did not mean the day had failed. It meant some outcomes still belonged to their authors.

kiln_p16_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_029.text: Peng put the decision into the archive beside its source packet. She did not file it among material failures merely because clay had broken. The incident series linked the process records, while the apprenticeship series held the access and learning decision. A worker seeking the technical lesson could find it without guessing from a moral tale. A future reviewer could see the full account without inventing a final qualification. Yue made the cross-reference carefully. She felt the archive become a kind of public memory, useful because it could hold connected facts without flattening every connection into a single cause.

kiln_p16_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_030.text: That evening the owner met the crew to explain the decision's practical effect. The cold roster would change, supervised teaching hours would be reserved and no one was obliged to act as Jian's friend. People were expected to work respectfully within the safe arrangement and report actual concerns. A worker asked whether the boy would receive favored lessons because he had caused trouble. The owner showed the existing teaching budget and the additional remedial hours funded from her incident provision. Ordinary learners' allocated instruction would remain intact. The numbers let workers see who would actually pay.

kiln_p16_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_031.text: Zhu volunteered to teach one paid cold session on rim defects but declined to supervise the live control path. She had a clear skill to share and a real limit. Luo accepted both without treating the refusal as disloyal. Jian thanked her privately afterward. She said the lesson would not be a gift that made his debt to her greater; it was ordinary agreed work. He looked surprised, then relieved. Yue had once believed kindness was clearest when nothing was priced. Here a named hour and a fair wage let kindness occur without disguising who would spend the time.

kiln_p16_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_032.text: Tan drafted the public notice and brought it to Peng. It gave the current safety schedule, customer arrangements and the supported finding without exposing unnecessary family details. The employment and apprenticeship remedy appeared in broad accurate terms, while private care information remained with its proper users. The storyteller complained again that nobody could tell whether the apprentice was saved or ruined. Tan said the notice's purpose was to tell people what they could safely do tomorrow. Yue smiled at the dry answer. It would not stop every dramatic retelling. It would give those who needed facts a place to start.

kiln_p16_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_033.text: On the next morning Jian arrived early for his cold shift and found that the new task board had no place to hide behind speed. He had three sample groups to sort, a copy check and a scheduled teacher hour. Finishing early would not open the live passage. He arranged his tools twice before beginning. Yue worked at the neighboring table on the public sample labels. Their friendship now included a boundary neither had needed to name before. She could share a laugh about a crooked jar. She could not wave him through a restriction because he looked lonely.

kiln_p16_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_034.text: The first remedial exercise used a harmless cold shutter and three described conditions. Jian solved the first by restoring the stop position. In the second, a changed support made the specified movement uncertain. He began proposing a substitute wedge and caught himself before reaching for it. The correct action was to stop, secure the cold model and ask for the revised task scope. Luo noted the pause without praising it as complete transformation. The boy had recognized one old impulse in a safe room. Learning to recognize it when embarrassed or hurried would require more than a neat answer.

kiln_p16_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_035.text: In the third exercise an apparent warning failure came from a misplaced sound screen. Jian wanted to move it immediately. Zhu asked what the operator at the other end had been told. He remembered the paired positions and asked for the cold comparison before changing the screen. Yue smiled at the small exchange. It was a skill made of noticing another worker's place in the mechanism. Jian wrote the lesson in his own words and avoided calling the model proof that he was ready for the live hall. The teacher signed only the observed cold task.

kiln_p16_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_036.text: Han's next care review found surface healing without deep damage. Tender movement still limited hot work. He could do longer cold shifts with rests and report any new change. The ordinary news made everyone cheerful until Han reminded them that longer work was not unrestricted work. He wanted to choose useful tasks rather than become a permanent object of concern. Peng assigned him inspection copies he knew well and paid the same agreed rate for the actual role. Yue carried his tea once, then stopped hovering when he asked her to. Care could become another form of crowding.

kiln_p16_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_037.text: The remake jars came out sound within the new ordinary schedule. The cooperative customer inspected capacity and stability before accepting the balance. She said the jars were ugly in exactly the reliable way she liked. Zhu took this as a compliment. Tan arranged the funded extra journey, obtained the receipt and closed that part of the customer account. The clinic pots required one further glaze correction unrelated to the vent damage, so their delivery remained open. Yue marked the difference carefully. The glaze correction still needed work, and belonged in a separate trial record.

kiln_p16_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_038.text: The glaze correction interested Zhu more than the hearing had. A surface that looked acceptable dry developed a fine roughness after the clinic's cleaning test. The body and firing had passed their defined checks; the glaze combination needed its own comparison under the intended ordinary use. She prepared small test tiles rather than recoat the whole stock on hope. Yue helped record the cleaning solution and contact time. The method had neither miraculous failure nor miraculous repair. It asked for a modest trial, a rejected combination and enough paid time to try the next mixture without hiding the first.

kiln_p16_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_039.text: Jian offered a suggestion based on an archive entry. Zhu asked him to retrieve the original instead of reciting its successful ending. It concerned a different body and a gentler cleaning process. He brought both the result and the limitation to the bench. The suggestion still helped them choose a comparison, though it could not certify the new glaze. Yue saw a useful learner begin to appear beneath the restricted worker without the restriction disappearing. He was allowed to contribute evidence. The contribution did not buy authority over the live process or make Han's tender arm an unfair memory.

kiln_p16_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_040.text: At the clinic delivery, Han's sister inspected the corrected pots without giving a speech about the workshop's honor. She asked where the cleaning notes would be kept and whether the next order would use the same qualified combination. Zhu supplied the record and explained the need to review any changed body or use. The sister thanked her, then asked Han whether he had eaten lunch. Yue laughed at the abrupt return to family. A public injury could attract solemn strangers; a sister still wanted to know why he had neglected the ordinary meal his recovering body actually needed.

kiln_p16_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_041.text: The owner began the independent credit check with former learners as promised. One arrived from a neighboring pottery with a folder of faded work slips. Another sent a letter saying she had no wish to return to the hall. Her records could be examined without requiring her presence. Peng prepared copies and retained the originals by agreement. Yue listened to the first interview and understood why the task needed time. People remembered hours as well as dates, kindness as well as missing signatures. The reviewer asked for names, dates and retained slips, then listened to the rest.

kiln_p16_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_042.text: Zhu's corrected credit stood during that check. The old incomplete final examination remained incomplete. A former teacher's new letter tried to describe her entire training as successful because he now felt ashamed of the missing entry. Peng refused the comforting overstatement and asked which work he had actually observed. The revised letter named trimming, cold layout and cooling observations, with the limits intact. Zhu read it and cried quietly. She wanted recognition strong enough to be useful. She did not want an invented live qualification that could place her injured hand beside a task she had never passed.

kiln_p16_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_043.text: Yue thought of the rank printed in her fourth-stage record. It had survived the shoulder injury as a history of earned channels, while her actual usable throughput had temporarily narrowed. She could have used the written rank to demand a larger task from someone unfamiliar with her care notes. Instead she kept the current recovery limit with the old assessment. That choice had once felt humiliating. Now she saw it beside Zhu's accurate letter and Jian's preserved skills. A record could respect a person's past without pretending the present body and permitted work were identical to it.

kiln_p16_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_044.text: The next anterior session used the same guarded receiving weight in a changed order after a arm comparison. Luo wanted to see whether the new route remained independently distinguishable when familiarity no longer supplied the sequence. Yue kept the anterior inward and outward return through foot, knee and hip separate from the established arms. The half-unit input over four breaths produced the known quarter useful unit and a clean release. Her reserve was measured after sampling rather than before its cost. The page still showed less than thirty-six usable units. She left the room tired in an ordinary, recoverable way.

kiln_p16_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_045.text: Her next morning's touch, grip and leg movement were normal. Su Yan reviewed the transmitted record when the circuit messenger arrived and asked for one quieter recovery week before beginning the distinct posterior route. She approved continued anterior work within the recovered limit, not a larger input because the sequence had changed successfully. Luo agreed. Yue resented the additional week until she saw the teacher's question about her sleep after the hearing. Body and attention had both worked hard. The method required a person who could recover between tasks, not merely a route that could produce a result once.

kiln_p16_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_046.text: The quiet week contained a muddy walk to the clay bank, two paid label sessions and an afternoon helping Zhu sort glaze colors. Yue took no personal input at the bank. She watched water darken the clay face and noticed how a promising dry sample could change after rain. The workers selected retained portions from the delivery area rather than the prettiest patch. She had expected rest to feel empty. Instead it gave her a slower education in the materials whose names cultivation records often treated as fixed. She pressed a thumb into the sample and left a shallow mark.

kiln_p16_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_047.text: At the bank Jian remained inside the allowed cold collection task under the assigned supervisor. A cart axle snagged a stone and someone asked him to fetch a live-yard lever. He declined and sent the supervisor for an approved ordinary tool. The delay embarrassed him in front of a younger worker. He later described the incident in his learning record, including the irritation. Luo said the irritation mattered because the safe action had survived it. Yue was glad no one transformed the moment into proof that trust was restored. It was a small reliable action in an unfinished course.

kiln_p16_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_048.text: The younger worker apologized for the casual request after seeing the roster limit. Jian said he could have explained it sooner rather than assume everyone knew the decision. They moved the retained clay together with the permitted cart. On the way back he told Yue that restrictions felt less like a wall when he could name their edge. She answered that the edge still existed on a day he disliked it. He nodded. Their conversations had lost some of the old quick joking, but gained pauses where one person could correct the other without immediately defending the entire friendship.

kiln_p16_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_049.text: Tan's sister came to the hall carrying the grain receipt that had once driven his foolish exchange. The household's winter balance was now ordinary and unremarkable, settled through actual wages and a small agreed family loan. She teased him for keeping three copies of every cart arrangement. He looked wounded until she saw the retained incident account and stopped. Yue heard them talking beside the gate about pride disguised as responsibility. The sister had never asked him to risk the workshop's fuel condition for her. He had wanted to arrive as the person who already solved the problem.

kiln_p16_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_050.text: That evening Tan told Yue he had been afraid that a straightforward request would reveal how little he controlled. The unauthorized exchange had let him act certain for half a day. It had cost others much longer. She thought of Jian's promised qualification date and her own dream of impossible bodily rescue. Different acts, different consequences, a recognizable wish to escape the moment of asking. Tan did not turn the resemblance into a universal theory. He returned to his receiving slate and wrote the actual question he needed approved. Yue copied that habit into her own quieter practice.

kiln_p16_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_051.text: The public cold sample visit took place at week's end. Yue's paid role was to show retained pieces and their use notes while Zhu and Luo handled the craft explanations. Children wanted the largest crack; former learners wanted the missing signatures. The reviewer arranged questions so neither audience swallowed the other. Jian sorted labels under supervision but did not perform a remorse speech for visitors. Han attended briefly with his care limit visible in the seating arrangement. The hall looked less grand than the proposed heroic notice. A former learner approached the table and unfolded a creased slip.

kiln_p16_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_052.text: A visitor asked why the archive kept an apparently sound teaching cup that had failed the guarded release test. Yue showed the external residual-warmth record and the physical boundaries that had prevented learner use. A flawless surface did not establish safe behavior under charge. The visitor then asked whether Qi could purify the cup. Luo explained that material defects and process history needed qualification; personal charge could add danger and cost, not erase them by desire. Yue felt pleased to say this beside the cup itself. The visitor tilted the cold cup toward the light, studying its deceptive surface.

kiln_p16_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_053.text: Another visitor asked whether the new control retainer proved no apprentice could ever interfere again. Luo said no. It improved the physical boundary and checks within its tested conditions. Supervision, reporting and independent review still mattered. The owner described access arrangements without publishing unnecessary details that would invite another experiment. Peng kept the question in the visit record. Yue watched the visitor accept a useful improvement that did not promise invulnerability. She wondered how much of her own cultivation ambition had begun as the wish to reach a stage where nobody could hurt anyone she loved.

kiln_p16_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_054.text: Near the end, Zhu invited former learners to mark which current task descriptions remained unclear. The slips filled a shallow ordinary bowl. One asked whether carrying a cooling slate counted as observing cooling; another asked who could challenge an assessor's missing signature. Peng answered what she could and assigned dated follow-up to the rest. The bowl had no cultivation role. Yue liked its use precisely because it held ordinary paper and made a public uncertainty visible. A shy learner waited until the crowd turned away, then slipped in a folded question.

kiln_p16_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_055.text: Jian read the visit questions later during his copying hour. He found several that resembled his own and looked almost angry with relief. The concerns had survived the finding against him. His act had not made them either forbidden or automatically correct. Yue said the general review still needed evidence and practical observation. He replied that he knew, then admitted he wished the distinction hurt less. She let the answer stand. Learning restraint had not made his desire disappear. It gave the desire routes that involved other people's consent, ordinary time and the possibility of an answer he would dislike.

kiln_p16_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p16_056.text: Han's next review allowed longer ordinary cold work and a gradual return to certain warm-room tasks away from the active grit path. Full hot-post clearance would wait. He celebrated by refusing the unusually soft lunch everyone had been offering him. Yue brought the regular bread and called him a difficult patient. He said difficult was a useful sign of improvement. Their laughter reached the doorway where Jian stood with a sample list. Han nodded for him to leave it on the bench.
